errors.english: Action refers to what has been transformed.
errors.why: ལས here is the ablative 'from' of the root verse (the deity transformed from the syllable), glossed as 'transformed', not 'action' (karma).

errors.english: the Great Black One [note: original: "Mahakala"] is extremely dark
errors.why: nag po chen po is glossed as a colour ('very black'), describing the deity's complexion, not the name Mahākāla.

note: A careful rendering of a Hevajra commentary passage; only the gloss of two root-text words is off.

errors.english: Precisely that is the pinnacle of existence
errors.why: ཡང་དག་པའི་མཐའ is bhūtakoṭi, 'the limit of reality', not bhavāgra 'the pinnacle of existence'.

fix.find: Precisely that is the pinnacle of existence
fix.replace: Precisely that is the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi)

note: Sound Yogācāra exposition of the three natures and three samādhis; one technical term rendered as a different, misleading term.

errors.english: do not eat without first assessing the amount of lentils or pulse provided for the illness
errors.why: This is the śaikṣa rule: out of greed (to get more), do not cover the curry/sauce [with rice], unless ill; nothing about assessing portions for an illness.

fix.find: do not eat without first assessing the amount of lentils or pulse provided for the illness [note: this refers to eating balanced portions suitable for one's health]
fix.replace: do not cover the curry [with rice], or [the rice with] curry, unless one is ill

errors.english: Not in a place of violent robbery where the current of safety is reversed. These instructions up to the word "ten"
errors.why: The rule is 'do not draw [water] against the current of a violent, sweeping stream'; མི་བཅུ is 'do not draw (water)', not the number ten.

fix.find: Not in a place of violent robbery where the current of safety is reversed. These instructions up to the word "ten"
fix.replace: Do not draw [water] against the current of a violent, sweeping stream. These instructions up to "do not draw"

errors.english: Do not teach while walking in front to one who is following behind.
errors.why: The roles are reversed: one coming behind should not teach Dharma to one who walks in front.

fix.find: Do not teach while walking in front to one who is following behind.
fix.replace: One who follows behind should not teach to one who walks in front.

errors.english: do not complain that the food is too hot or too cold, and do not spit while eating
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'too bitter, too cold' etc. and has only 'do not grumble about the food'; 'do not spit while eating' is not there and 'hot' is not ཁ.

note: The plain rules are mostly right, but three Vinaya rules are mistranslated (one with roles reversed) and the explanatory gloss misreads 'do not draw' as 'ten'.

errors.english: craving causes the childish being to be fully purified [note: or prepared for rebirth]
errors.why: In context (cf. སྲེད་པའི་ཀུན་ཏུ་སྦྱོར་བ on the next side) craving binds/yokes the immature being to those destinies; 'purified' inverts the sense.

note: A faithful rendering of the Yogācārabhūmi-type list of differences between the receptacle and birth cycles; one verb misread.

errors.why: The commentary (previous side) explains Jinajik as 'he who produces the Victors' / 'victor over birth', not 'Victor of Victors'.

errors.english: (Arolik) the seed syllable or name associated with the Lotus Family
errors.why: Ārolik is a name of the Lotus-family Buddha (Amitābha), not a seed syllable; the note is misleading.

note: Good rendering of the Nāmasaṃgīti-type etymologies of the five Buddhas; two explanatory glosses are loose.
A faithful rendering of terse pramāṇa sub-commentary, with lemmata and argument structure kept.

errors.why: རང་མཚན here is 'one's own name' (the vajra-name then uttered), not the epistemological 'self-characteristic'.

errors.english: This very act is the sign of the first action and of slightly coming under the power of primordial wisdom.
errors.why: ལས་དང་པོ refers to the beginner (ādikarmika) stage, not a 'first action'.

note: Generally accurate tantric ritual commentary; one technical term mistaken in the naming rite.

errors.english: Although they have attained the eighth stage and have become thoroughly familiar with it in that way, they have not reached the "Stage of Thinning"
errors.why: The comparison is: as one who reaches the eighth stage is irreversible, so these, having become well familiarised, [stand on that level] and not on the 'thinned' stages (2–7); the English says eighth-stage bodhisattvas have not reached a lower stage, which is incoherent.

errors.english: [note: original: བསྲབས་པའི་ས་ (rab-pé-sa); refers to the Tanu-bhumi, where afflictions are thinned]
errors.why: The phonetic 'rab-pé-sa' is wrong (bsrabs pa'i sa, 'sab-pé-sa').

note: Accurate on the signs of irreversibility; the comparison with the eighth stage is garbled.

errors.english: A deep and perfect distillation of the six types of relief
errors.why: དབུགས་དབྱུང here is ucchvāsa, the textual sections/chapters (six sections drawn from the Māyājāla), not 'relief'.

note: Opening of a Nāmasaṃgīti maṇḍala rite, rendered well apart from one term in the verse.

errors.english: are sealed as the reflections of the (mudras) symbolic hand gestures or seals
errors.why: The mudrās are the agent: they seal all beings as their own image (reflection), rather than beings being the reflections of the mudrās.

note: A faithful rendering of the maṇḍala-feast and entry passage; one case relation shifted.
